title: Natural Language Processing for Human Resources: A Survey

bias_targets.methodology: The survey reviews existing literature that measures gender bias by analyzing word embeddings for associations between gender pronouns and specific job titles (e.g., "she" with "nurse"), as well as evaluating gendered differences in system-generated texts like job advertisements and reference letters.

The paper summarizes studies that use person names as proxies for sensitive demographic attributes (such as race and gender) to measure how these names influence downstream LLM-generated outcomes, including reference letters and algorithmic hiring decisions.
